places.name: Hàn Diễm Khẩu
places.size: A crack in a high glacier about 300 m long that breathes pale blue flames, with a glassy scorched lip about 40 m wide and a sulphur stain about 400 m long; no buildings, at most a tiny cairn and a rope line.
places.where: Region 7, high on the ice mountains at about 2.7 km. On the map a grey and white range of snowy parallel ridges with a small dark volcanic crater at the centre and a blue sea bay at the upper left with a forested coast and some dark forest at the upper right. Lava vent (địa hỏa tinh) held by Băng Tâm Các. Nearest: Hồi Lộ Phong 152 km, Bão Tuyết Phong 215 km.
places.imagined: A clear cold afternoon. A long crack in the glacier breathes pale blue flames that dance over the snow without melting it, the ice around the lip glassy and scorched dark, and downwind a yellow stain of sulphur.
places.subject: The place: Hàn Diễm Khẩu, the Cold Flame Vent, a crack in a high glacier that breathes pale blue fire. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a vast range of grey rock ridges and white snowfields runs in parallel folds across the frame, a small black volcanic crater in the centre, blue sea and a forested coast at the upper left and dark forest strips at the upper right, glacier ice glittering between the ridges. Signature element: in the centre of the frame a long crack about three hundred metres long splits the glacier, its edges forming a glassy, dark scorched lip about forty metres wide of smooth black-brown ice like polished obsidian, and from the crack rise pale blue flames in a long jagged curtain, some as tall as a house, flickering and leaning with the wind, glowing against the white snow without melting it; faint heat shimmer rises above them. Downwind to one side a bright yellow sulphur stain spreads about four hundred metres across the snow in a long fan with a faint pale yellow dusting. The ice around is cracked and treacherous, with thin blue crevasses radiating from the crack. A single rope line and a tiny cairn of dark stones stand on the safe side with two tiny figures in grey looking on, one with a pole testing the ice. Light and season: clear cold afternoon in winter, golden light from the upper left on the ice and the sulphur, the blue flames glowing against it, deep blue shadows in the crevasses, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Tầm Kiếm Đường
places.size: A lodge of about 30 hunters and guides, all men, founded 1162: one large timber lodge and about 20 sheds, stables and storehouses in about 200 m at the forest's edge; a wall of maps inside; small, rough and open to any man.
places.where: Region 7, forest below the southern massif at about 140 m, on a coast. On the map a forested peninsula running from the upper right to the lower left between a bright turquoise bay at the top and a deeper sea at the left, with a grey rocky slope in the middle and a thin river branching at the centre. Vassal of Băng Tâm Các, neutral, no lean. Nearest: Hào Trư Cương beast lair 103 km, Hòe Âm Trấn 177 km, Hàn Thiết Khoáng mine 215 km.
places.imagined: Dawn. A timber lodge sits where the forest meets the slope, a map wall visible through its open door, a guide at the gate with a notch-filed sword at his hip, and a hunting party is setting off up a stream toward the caves.
places.subject: The place: Tầm Kiếm Đường, the Sword-Seeking Hall, a hunters' lodge at the forest's edge under a mountain massif. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a forested peninsula of pine and mixed forest runs from the upper right to the lower left, a bright turquoise bay at the top and a deeper blue sea along the left, a grey rocky slope of scree and cliffs rising in the lower middle, a thin river branching in two at the centre of the frame and running into the bay. The lodge: in a clearing at the forest edge near the river fork stands one large timber lodge about forty metres long with a long steep roof of dark shingle and a deep porch, around which about twenty smaller buildings, stables for a dozen pack ponies, a smokehouse, drying racks for hides and meat, a cave-gear store with ropes and ladders hanging in bundles, sleeping sheds, a wood yard and a small training ground with a sword rack. Signature element: through the lodge's open double door a whole wall of hand-drawn maps shows pale against the dark inside, hundreds of sheets pinned in rows, and on the slope behind the lodge, in the grey rock face, dozens of small dark cave mouths, each marked with a tiny cairn or a strip of red cloth, a long pale trail of cairns winding up to them from the lodge. Life at scale: a party of about eight tiny hunters with packs and ropes setting off up the trail, a guide with a notch-filed sword at the gate, pack ponies being loaded, smoke from the cookhouse. Light and season: clear dawn in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the lodge roof and the cliff, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Băng Tâm Các (the Desert Pavilion, Cựu Các)
places.size: The old seat of a great sword sect (tier 2), now the sect's outer hall for the desert, Cựu Các: a domain about 3 km across on red badland ridges, about 150 buildings with a tall celadon pavilion tower about 60 m high; once home to hundreds, now a few dozen sect disciples and a few hundred servants, oasis children recruits and artisans.
places.where: Region 7, high badlands at the desert's edge at about 900 m. On the map a rolling ochre and olive upland with a ridge of orange-red eroded badlands running diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, a dark green forest north of it and a black volcanic cone at the top right corner. Lord's old seat (Earth, Metal), founded 440 by Tần Ngưng Sương; the seat moved to Hồ Thiên Phái (place 214) in 470 and this is now the Desert Pavilion. Nearest: Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền 103 km, Tống Khách Thị 214 km.
places.imagined: Midsummer at the desert's edge. Even now frost rims the eaves of a tall white pavilion tower of stacked celadon-glazed roofs, a thin cold mist spills from the round well-house at its foot, and an oasis child is being led up the pale stone terraces.
places.subject: The place: the Desert Pavilion, the old seat of the great ice-sword sect Băng Tâm Các, on red badlands. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a rolling upland of ochre grass and olive scrub fills the frame, a long ridge of orange-red eroded badlands with grey rock teeth running diagonally across the middle, a dark green forest across the top and a black volcanic cone far off in the upper right corner. The seat: pale stone terraces climb the red ridge in long flights to a tall white pavilion tower of many stacked celadon-green glazed roofs, about sixty metres high and the tallest outline in the whole land, its eaves edged with white frost even in the heat; around it about a hundred and fifty buildings of pale stone with green glazed roofs, great halls, long colonnaded dormitories, practice courts of white flagstones, kitchens, store halls and walled gardens on the terraces, with gate towers and bridges over the red gullies; the domain's outer walls run along the badland crest. Signature element: at the foot of the pavilion stands a round white well-house with a thin cold mist spilling from its door and spreading in a pale pool over the red ground, the water below it keeping ice all year, and a white frost fan around it on the red dust. Life at scale: lines of tiny servants carrying water up the terraces, a train of pack camels in the lower yard, about twenty small children in a line being led up by two figures in white, sword drill by a few disciples. Light and season: bright midsummer morning, golden light from the upper left on the white walls and red ridges, the frost glittering, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Dạ Quang Môn
places.size: A demonic-path (ma đạo) sect of about 120 riders and their families, founded 970: a square rammed-earth fort about 140 m on a side with about 45 buildings inside, horse lines of some 150 horses and sabre racks outside, a tall pillar over the gate; compact, bare and hoof-trampled.
places.where: Region 7, open steppe at sea level. On the map golden-brown rolling grassland with a thin river winding down the middle to a small estuary and the sea at the lower right, a green forested belt at the lower left. Vassal of Băng Tâm Các since 1121, Earth 34 %, Fire 32 %. Nearest: Xích Sa Mạch spirit vein 75 km, Cô Thành ruin 125 km, Lục Ba Đàm lake 152 km. Hạng Dạ Bôi founded it among desert raiders.
places.imagined: Dusk on the steppe. The squat red fort stands in a ring of trampled bare ground, horse lines and sabre racks all round, and over its gate a great stone cup on a pillar glows faint green in the dark.
places.subject: The place: Dạ Quang Môn, the Night-Light Gate, a fort of raiders turned escorts on an open steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; golden-brown rolling steppe grassland fills the frame, a thin river winding down the middle from the top toward a small estuary and the blue sea at the lower right, a green forested belt at the lower left, faint caravan tracks crossing the grass. The fort: a squat square fort of red rammed earth about a hundred and forty metres on a side, with a three-roof timber gate tower the tallest outline, bastions at the corners, and about forty-five low flat-roofed buildings inside around a parade yard, barracks, a smithy, a war hall, a granary and a well; outside the walls on every side the steppe is trampled bare for a hundred metres by hooves, with long horse lines of about a hundred and fifty horses on picket ropes, racks of curved sabres in rows under lean-to roofs, felt tents of the families, and a ring of black fire pits. Signature element: over the gate, on a tall stone pillar about twelve metres high, stands a great stone cup, carved from a pale stone that glows faint green, a small green star above the dark fort; the glow lies in a faint pool on the gate's red wall and on the ground below. Life at scale: about forty tiny riders in a column returning along a caravan track escorting a long line of loaded camels, young riders in a ring around a cup-of-light, children with ponies. Light and season: dusk in late summer, the last golden light from the upper left on the fort walls and the horse lines, long soft shadows toward the lower right, the stone cup glowing green.

places.name: Trường Vân Thành
places.size: A walled harbour city of about 20,000 roofs and perhaps 100,000 people, walls about 3 km by 2.2 km at a river mouth, with a roofed caravan gallery about 1.8 km long running straight from the land gate to the docks and a shimmering ward formation over the walls.
places.where: Region 7, edge of the desert where a river meets the sea, at sea level. On the map golden-brown grassland and scrub with a river winding from the top down to a small estuary and a large bay of blue sea at the lower right, dark green forest at the lower left. Băng Tâm Các city founded 470, its door to the sea. Nearest: Cô Thành ruin 125 km, Lục Ba Đàm 175 km, Liên Đường Thôn 190 km.
places.imagined: A cloudy afternoon under long clouds over snow mountains far off. Goods pass from camel to ship through the long roofed gallery without seeing the sun, and a faint shimmer of a ward shows over the walls.
places.subject: The place: Trường Vân Thành, the Long Cloud city, a walled harbour city at the desert's edge. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; golden-brown grassland and scrub with desert sand on the landward side fills the upper frame, a river winding down from the top into a small estuary and a large bay of blue sea at the lower right, dark green forest at the lower left. The city: a great rectangular wall of grey stone about three kilometres long, with a gate tower of three roofs at each end of the main axis and a dozen smaller gate towers, enclosing some twenty thousand grey-tile roofs in districts of tight lanes, caravanserais with camel yards, ship chandlers' rows, officers' compounds and taverns; a harbour with long quays, a sea mole and about two hundred ships. Signature element: straight through the middle of the city runs a long continuous roofed caravan gallery about eighteen hundred metres long, from the land gate to the docks, a single long gabled roof of grey tile like the spine of a great animal, so that goods pass from camel to ship without seeing the sun; its inside is a pale line of lantern light, and a train of camels enters at the land gate while cranes lift crates at the sea end. Over the walls a faint silver shimmer of the ward formation lies like a thin ring. Life at scale: about a hundred camels in the land yard, caravan guards in the taverns, porters in lines, ships at anchor. Light and season: cloudy afternoon in early autumn, a break in the cloud letting golden light from the upper left onto the gallery roof, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hồi Lan Thành
places.size: A harbour city of about 14,000 roofs and perhaps 70,000 people, walls about 2.4 km by 1.8 km, built behind a long curved breakwater about 1.5 km long that hooks out into the sea; sand-coloured walls and pale grey roofs.
places.where: Region 7, desert coast at sea level. On the map a dry ochre and orange-brown grassland and badlands on the left, a straight clean coast running top to bottom with deep blue sea at the right and a green forested fringe at the top. Băng Tâm Các city founded 760 after the Desert Road War. Nearest: Ôn Thạch Thang hot spring 103 km, Khổ Thủy Trì 318 km.
places.imagined: Noon on the desert coast. Waves roll against the long curved breakwater and turn back on themselves, white surf curling along its outer face, while ships from the south crowd the still water inside the hook.
places.subject: The place: Hồi Lan Thành, the Returning Wave city, a harbour city on the desert coast behind a curved breakwater. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a dry ochre and orange-brown country of grassland and eroded badlands fills the left of the frame, a straight clean coast runs top to bottom, deep blue sea fills the right, a green forested fringe at the very top. The city: a rectangular city of sand-coloured walls and pale grey-tile roofs about two and a half kilometres long, a gate tower the tallest roofline, enclosing about fourteen thousand low roofs in regular blocks, long low warehouses of pale stone along the harbour, a rice market, merchant halls with courtyards, a customs hall and a lighthouse tower on the breakwater root; broad dusty avenues and shade awnings. Signature element: from the harbour a long curved stone breakwater about fifteen hundred metres long hooks out into the sea like a great crooked arm, its outer face lined with white surf curling back from it, turning the waves back on themselves, while inside the hook the water is a still pale turquoise, crowded with about sixty ships from the south, high-sterned sea junks and rice barges moored in rows and others tying up at the quays. Life at scale: porters carrying rice sacks in lines along the quay, dockworkers on the breakwater, caravans arriving on the desert road from the left. Light and season: bright noon in late summer, strong golden light from the upper left on the sand-coloured walls, short crisp shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Ngư Đàm Thôn
places.size: A small oasis village of about 20 flat-roofed mud-brick houses with about 40 square fish ponds on a grid about 400 m across, perhaps 100 people, with a salt-boat landing.
places.where: Region 7, desert coast at sea level. On the map golden-brown rolling dry grassland with a thin green strip above a bitter salt shore, deep blue sea along the bottom with a small island at the lower edge. Băng Tâm Các village, Water, Earth. Nearest: Hoàng Thổ Mạch 180 km, Âu Lộ Thôn 293 km, Chiên Trướng Thôn 325 km. The desert's only fish.
places.imagined: Noon heat. A neat grid of square fish ponds edged with mud brick sparkles in the oasis behind a bitter salt shore, date palms shade the dikes, and children with wooden clappers chase herons off the shallows.
places.subject: The place: Ngư Đàm Thôn, the Fish Pond village, a small oasis of fish ponds behind a salt shore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; golden-brown rolling dry grassland fills the upper frame, a thin green band of the oasis at its edge above a pale bitter salt shore, deep blue sea along the lower edge with white surf, a small island at the lower edge. The village: about twenty low flat-roofed houses of mud brick lining the dikes between the ponds, each with a small yard, a few shade awnings, a water-jar yard and a clay oven; a small mud-brick hall with a larger flat roof; a tiny landing at the shore for salt boats with two small boats and a salt-drying flat of white crust beside it. Signature element: a neat grid of about forty square fish ponds, each about thirty metres on a side, edged with mud brick and bright blue-green against the dry ground, shaded in places by about sixty date palms; the grid is the only geometry in the landscape, so that the oasis looks like a chequerboard of water. Herons stand in the shallows. Life at scale: about ten tiny villagers working along the dikes with nets, children with wooden clappers running at the herons, a man filling water jars with carp at a pond edge, a camel waiting with jar panniers at the village edge. Light and season: hot noon in summer, strong golden light from the upper left making the ponds glitter, short crisp shadows beneath the palms toward the lower right.

places.name: Liên Đường Thôn
places.size: A steppe village of about 12 mud-brick houses with reed roofs and a wooden viewing pier, perhaps 60 people, beside a hollow of about 8 lotus ponds about 400 m across.
places.where: Region 7, open steppe at sea level inland from a bay. On the map green and gold rolling steppe with a river winding at the left edge, a small branched lagoon at the upper middle and a sea bay at the right edge, dark forest at the upper right. A Dạ Quang Môn village. Nearest: Lục Ba Đàm 75 km, Mã Minh Thôn 158 km, Cô Thành 168 km. Lotus ponds have bloomed here since 560.
places.imagined: High summer. A hollow of spring-fed ponds blooms pink and white with lotus, a wooden viewing pier reaches over the leaves, and a caravan halts on the rise above just to look.
places.subject: The place: Liên Đường Thôn, the Lotus Pond village, a few houses among lotus ponds in the open steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; green and gold rolling steppe fills the frame, a river winding at the left edge, a small branched lagoon at the upper middle, a bay of blue sea at the right edge, dark forest at the upper right, a faint caravan track crossing the grass. In the middle a green hollow about four hundred metres across lies sunk in the golden steppe, its floor filled with about eight spring-fed ponds of different shapes, joined by narrow channels, and every pond is thick with lotus, round leaves in many shades of green and pink and white blossoms by the thousand. The village: about twelve low houses of mud brick with reed roofs on the banks between the ponds, each with a small yard and drying racks of lotus root and seed pods, a tiny shrine; a small wooden viewing pier about forty metres long reaches out over the leaves. Signature element: the lotus hollow, a lush pink-and-white-and-green blaze set in the dry gold of the steppe, bright as a jewel; on the rise above, a caravan of about twenty camels has halted just to look, tiny figures standing in a line. Life at scale: two villagers in a flat punt cutting lotus, a child handing a seed to a traveller, a rider watering a horse at the far pond. Light and season: high summer morning, golden light from the upper left making the lotus glow, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Mã Minh Thôn
places.size: A nomad-herders' village of about 25 felt tents and flat-roofed mud houses ringed by about 10 round dry-stone horse corrals each about 30 m across, perhaps 130 people with about 400 horses.
places.where: Region 7, steppe behind the range, at about 30 m. On the map green and gold rolling steppe with a river winding down at the left, a small branched lagoon at the upper right and a sea bay at the right edge, dark forest at the left edge. Băng Tâm Các village. Nearest: Mục Thảo Mạch 125 km, Liên Đường Thôn 158 km, Lục Ba Đàm 195 km. A sandstorm buried the old wells in 1050 and the village moved east.
places.imagined: Morning. The neigh of horses carries far over the grass, round corrals of piled dry stone ring the camp, and to the west a low hump of sand covers the old wells where the village once stood.
places.subject: The place: Mã Minh Thôn, the Horse Neigh village, a nomad herders' village on the steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; green and gold rolling steppe fills the frame, a river winding down at the left with dark forest beyond it, a small branched lagoon at the upper right and a sea bay at the right edge, a mountain range far at the horizon. The village: about twenty-five round felt tents and flat-roofed mud houses scattered in loose clusters with cook fires between them, a long open sales yard with hitching rails, saddle racks and tack sheds, a well with a trough, and a stone watch post; the grass around is trampled flat. Signature element: about ten round corrals of piled dry stone, each about thirty metres across, ring the camp like a necklace, and inside them tiny horse specks, about four hundred in total, chestnut, grey and black, with a few foals; a herd of another hundred is being driven at a gallop across the steppe with a dust trail behind them. To one side, a low hump of pale sand about a hundred metres across lies over the old buried wells, half grassed over, with a few weathered well-posts sticking out. Life at scale: herders on horseback, children on ponies, a buyer inspecting a horse, women milking mares. Light and season: bright morning in early summer, golden light from the upper left on the horses and the felt tents, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Viên Đề Hạp
places.size: A narrow gorge about 8 km long and 150 m wide between walls about 400 m high, with a timber plank road pinned to one wall for the whole length; no buildings, at most a tiny waystation shed at one end.
places.where: Region 7, high mountains at about 200 m at the gorge floor, Cô Yên Mạc. On the map a rugged grey and white mountain range with deep clefts and a river winding diagonally from the upper left to the lower right in a ravine, orange-brown scree pockets and a few tiny blue tarns, golden steppe at the right edge. Belongs to no sect, the plank road is mended by whoever needs it. Nearest: Hắc Ưng Phong 215 km, Xích Vũ Phong 251 km.
places.imagined: Dawn. Mist fills the gorge floor, a thin timber plank road pinned to the cliff face runs the length of one wall, and gibbons swing in the vines on both banks crying without end.
places.subject: The place: Viên Đề Hạp, the Gibbon Cry Gorge, a narrow gorge with a plank road pinned to the cliff. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a rugged range of grey and white mountains with parallel folds fills the frame, a narrow dark gorge cutting diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, its walls steep and grey, draped with green vines and hanging moss, orange-brown scree pockets on the shoulders, a few tiny blue tarns on the heights and golden steppe visible at the right edge. A white-water river rushes through the bottom of the gorge, partly hidden by drifting dawn mist that fills the gorge floor like cotton. Signature element: along one wall of the gorge a thin timber plank road, a narrow ledge of planks pinned on pegs and cross-braces driven into the rock, runs the entire length, in places a few metres above the water, in places a hundred metres up, with a gap bridged by a hanging rope at one corner, its pale line clear on the dark cliff; a tiny waystation shed with a plank roof perches at one end. Dark gibbon specks, about thirty, swing in the vines on both walls and a few sit on the planks. Life at scale: a caravan of about ten laden pack animals and drivers with their ears stopped with wax moving single file along the planks. Light and season: dawn in early autumn, golden light from the upper left striking the upper walls while the gorge floor is in blue mist, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Cô Thành
places.size: A ruined square fortress about 200 m on a side on a white salt pan about 3 km across that was once a desert lake; about 40 slumped buildings inside walls fire-glazed black, one corner tower still full height; once a garrison of a few hundred, empty since its fall.
places.where: Region 7, steppe at sea level. On the map golden-brown steppe with a river winding down from the top to a small branched estuary and a blue sea bay at the lower right, dark green forest at the left. Former city/fortress held by Băng Tâm Các, raised 520 to guard the caravan road; destroyed in the Desert Road War, held out two years in 724-726. Nearest: Lục Ba Đàm 106 km, Dạ Quang Môn 125 km, Trường Vân Thành 125 km.
places.imagined: A hard white noon. A square fortress with walls glazed black and cracked by fire stands on a salt pan that was once a lake, one corner tower still at full height, salt crust climbing the wall bases like frost.
places.subject: The place: Cô Thành, the Lone Fortress, a fire-ruined fortress on a white salt pan in the desert. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a flat white salt pan, the bed of a vanished desert lake, fills the middle of the frame with a faintly crazed crust and a few pale shoreline rings, golden-brown steppe around it, a thin river and a small estuary far at the lower right, dark forest at the left. The ruin: a square fortress about two hundred metres on a side, its walls fire-glazed black and cracked like burnt pottery, four corner towers of which one still rises to its full height, jagged and glassy at the top, and three have slumped into rubble heaps; about forty buildings inside, barracks and a granary, roofless and charred, around a dry well with a heap of white salt stones beside it. Signature element: the salt crust creeping up the wall bases like white frost, thick and bright on the lower three metres, and the lone standing tower with its dark glazed face. A dry caravan track runs across the white to the fortress's broken gate, marked by a few pale wheel ruts and a line of cairns. Life at scale: no inhabitants; two tiny travellers sitting in the gate's shadow, one camel at the foot of the tower. Light and season: hard white noon in late summer, strong golden light from the upper left making the salt glare, short crisp black shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền
places.size: A spirit-vein spring and a smiths' forge complex of about 25 forge sheds and a washing pool, in a basin about 500 m across in red badlands; a few dozen smiths; small and smoky.
places.where: Region 7, high mountain at about 700 m, steppe and desert edge. On the map orange-red eroded badland ridges with grey rock fins running diagonally across golden sand dunes, olive grass and dark forest at the top. Spirit vein held by Băng Tâm Các (Earth, Fire), the Sword-Washing Spring, where Trấn Sa Đường's smiths work. Nearest: Băng Tâm Các 103 km, Trấn Sa Đường 293 km, Tống Khách Thị 304 km.
places.imagined: Afternoon in the red hills. Blades are quenched in the spring's cold water in clouds of steam, forge smoke rises from a row of low sheds, and pale dunes lie beyond the red ridges.
places.subject: The place: Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền, the Sword-Washing Spring, a forge on a cold spring in red badlands. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; orange-red eroded badland ridges with grey rock fins run diagonally across the frame, golden sand dunes in the lower half with long wind ripples, olive grass and scrub pockets between, dark green forest at the top edge. In the middle a small basin among the red ridges, about five hundred metres across, holds the spring: a round clear pool about forty metres across of startlingly cold blue-green water ringed by a pale mineral rim, fed by a thin stream from a cleft and spilling out into a channel that winds down toward the dunes. The forge: about twenty-five low sheds of red stone with flat and low-pitched roofs, open on one side, around the pool, each with a chimney and a quenching trough fed from the spring channel, a long hall for the smiths' meals, a charcoal yard, racks of finished blades in rows under awnings, and a small stone shrine. Signature element: the clouds of white steam that rise from quenching troughs and from the pool's edge whenever a red-hot blade is dipped, drifting across the red hills, and the line of tiny figures along the pool's rim with blades held in tongs; plumes of dark forge smoke rise beyond them. Life at scale: about thirty tiny smiths at forges and troughs, a camel train carrying charcoal, apprentices carrying water. Light and season: afternoon in autumn, warm golden light from the upper left making the red ridges glow, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Trấn Sa Đường
places.size: A walled caravanserai of a guard sect of about 80 guards, smiths and grooms from the guard families, founded 1125: a rectangular compound about 160 m by 110 m with about 40 buildings, camel pens for about 100 camels, a well, a watchtower and a long hall; compact and practical.
places.where: Region 7, open steppe and dune country at about 380 m. On the map pale golden sand dunes between olive-green steppe with scrub, orange-red badland ridges at the top and right, a small grey rock outcrop in the middle. Vassal of Băng Tâm Các, Earth, Metal; its forge is at Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền. Nearest: Liệt Dương Huyệt 269 km, Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền 293 km, Chiên Trướng Thôn 305 km. Founded to guard the caravans and to watch the raiders who ride escort.
places.imagined: Late afternoon. A caravan is arriving at a walled caravanserai on the steppe, camel pens filling, the watchtower throwing a long shadow over the sand, and the guard families sitting down to eat together in the long hall.
places.subject: The place: Trấn Sa Đường, the Sand-Holding Hall, a walled caravanserai of caravan guards on the steppe. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; pale golden sand dunes with long wind ripples lie between pockets of olive-green steppe and scrub, orange-red badland ridges at the top and right, a grey rock outcrop near the middle, and a faint caravan road crossing the frame. The caravanserai: a rectangular compound of pale mud-brick and stone walls about a hundred and sixty metres long, with a tall square watchtower at one corner the tallest outline, a gatehouse with a big arched gate, and inside about forty buildings: a long hall where the guard families eat together, with a great flat roof, long stable ranges, store rooms and rooms for travellers around a large central yard with a stone-curbed well, camel pens outside the wall for about a hundred camels in tidy rows, wagon sheds, a small smithy for repairs, and a plain sword rack court. Signature element: a long caravan of about sixty camels and a dozen wagons arrives along the road in a line, their long shadows crossing the dunes, tiny guards on horseback at its head and tail, the first animals already entering the gate; the watchtower's shadow falls across the sand like a long thin hand. Life at scale: grooms taking animals, guards on the wall, smiths at their work, children on a camel. Light and season: late afternoon in autumn, warm golden light from the upper left on the walls and the dunes, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Đà Linh Trấn
places.size: A caravan-road town of about 1,200 roofs, a low earth-brick town about 500 m by 350 m with a toll gate on a river, roughly 5,500 people; a hub where Dạ Quang's escorts are hired.
places.where: Region 7, steppe at the edge of the mountains at about 30 m. On the map a steep grey rocky mountain range at the left with dark forest above, a river winding down in a smooth S-curve through golden sand dunes and olive grass, orange scree at the right. Băng Tâm Các town, Earth, Fire. Nearest: Phong Sa Nhãn spirit vein 112 km, Mộc Kiều Thôn 168 km, Viên Nhật Huyệt 190 km. The escort road runs from here to Hồi Lan.
places.imagined: Morning at the escort board. Trains gather in the yards, a toll bar stands across the road at the river crossing, and Dạ Quang's captains post their legs on the board beside the gate.
places.subject: The place: Đà Linh Trấn, the Camel-Bell town, a toll-and-escort town on the caravan road beside a river. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a steep grey rocky mountain range with dark conifer forest above it fills the left of the frame, a river winding in a smooth S-curve through the middle between golden sand dunes and olive grass, orange scree pockets at the right, a faint road running down the valley. The town: a low walled town of about twelve hundred flat- and low-pitched roofs of earth brick in sand-coloured blocks, a wall about five hundred metres long with two gates, a toll bridge with a bar across it at the river and a gate house with a large notice board at its side, long caravan yards with camel pens, warehouses with grain sacks and bales, inns with courtyard stables, a market lane, a hall of the escort captains with a deep roof, a well. Signature element: in the yards beside the town several caravans are gathering at once, about five hundred camels in strings and rows with their loads stacked beside them, riders of the escort in groups at the board, and the long road leading out, hundreds of pale prints in the sand; a few banners without marks hang on poles at the toll bar. Life at scale: tiny caravaneers loading camels, a captain reading a leg, children on a bridge, a toll collector at the bar. Light and season: bright morning in early autumn, golden light from the upper left on the earth walls and the sand dunes, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Mai Sa Bảo
places.size: A ruined mountain fort of about 40 buried and half-buried buildings in a footprint about 250 m by 180 m under a drift of sand, with a few tower tops showing; once a garrison of about 150; under it, it is said, a hoard of stones, silver and a century of caravans.
places.where: Region 7, mountain valley at about 720 m. On the map a steep grey rocky range with a white cloud at the upper left, olive and golden slopes and dunes at the lower right, a river winding at the right edge, an orange ravine in the centre, dark forest at the top. Former fort held by Dạ Quang Môn. Nearest: Hồng Thạch Phong 90 km, Dương Chi Khoáng 112 km, Ngưng Băng Bảo 152 km. A sandstorm buried it in 1050.
places.imagined: A hard clear morning after a wind. Sand has drifted over the old walls so that only the tops of two towers and a curtain of battlement show, and one corner has just been uncovered by the storm.
places.subject: The place: Mai Sa Bảo, the Buried Sand fort, a mountain fort buried by a sandstorm. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a steep grey rocky mountain range fills the left and upper part of the frame with a drift of white cloud at its upper left and a belt of dark conifer along the top, a narrow orange-red ravine running down its middle, olive and golden slopes and dunes at the lower right and a river winding at the right edge. The ruin: in a mountain valley a great drift of pale golden sand about two hundred and fifty metres long has buried a fort, so that its shape is only suggested by ripples: the tops of two stone watchtowers poke out of the sand, a long stretch of crenellated curtain wall shows along one side and the roofs of a few barrack halls show as dark ridges, with the rest a smooth dune that hides about forty buildings. Signature element: at one corner the wind has just uncovered a heap of dark stone, a broken doorway and the edge of a stone-lined cellar full of sand, with scattered glints of metal and a dark gap leading down, and four tiny figures, riders and a guard from different parties, stand around it at a cautious distance, their camels behind them and their long shadows crossing the dune. A pale track of footprints leads from the river. Light and season: hard clear early morning in autumn, golden light from the upper left raking the sand ripples into long fine lines, deep blue shadows in the ravine, long soft shadows toward the lower right.
